question: Shared: predicting which cognitively normal ADNI older adults will progress to MCI, from baseline hippocampal structural T1 MRI (MRI channel in both). P-132 adds ADAS-Cog11/13 scores to hippocampal radiomic features. P-177 uses hippocampal surface multivariate morphometry with patch-based sparse coding. Horizon, case definition, control construction, features and validation differ. Condition 1 allows these, so they are recorded as candidate explanations.

figures.P-132: 175 ADNI NC (125 stable/50 progressed to MCI within 7 years), stratified 80/20 split; test set 25 sNC + 10 pNC = 35. Test accuracy: LightGBM 0.74 (26/35 = 0.743), SVM 0.77 (27/35), LR 0.73, RF 0.74; test AUC 0.80 (LightGBM). Training accuracy 0.79-0.81 (the record's 'Acc 79' is the LightGBM training figure). No intervals printed. Wilson, 26/35: 0.579-0.858; 27/35: 0.610-0.879. Training 0.81 over 140: 0.737-0.866. Test AUC 0.80, Hanley-McNeil (10/25): Q1 = 0.6667, Q2 = 0.7111, SE = 0.0918, CI 0.620-0.980.
figures.P-177: ADNI cohort, 60 progressors to amnestic MCI in about 2 years vs 60 matched nonprogressors (cognitively unimpaired at least 4 years); leave-one-out CV (Table 2): accuracy 0.92, sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.97. Mean over 10 patch selections: 0.90 +/- 0.01 (Table 5). No intervals printed. Wilson, 110/120: 0.853-0.954; for 0.90 over 120: 0.833-0.942. Arizona cohort 0.92 (n = 38); combined cohorts 0.90 (158, 5-fold CV). Hippocampal volume alone, same ADNI design: 0.72 (Table 4).

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-132 reports no result at a 2-year horizon, none for amnestic MCI only, and none on an extreme-group matched sample. P-177 reports no result at a 7-year horizon or on an unselected cohort. Neither paper evaluates the other's feature set. P-177's hippocampal-volume baseline (0.72) is closer to P-132's accuracy, but it is P-177's design with a third feature set, not P-132's condition. It shows that representation moves accuracy within P-177's design; it does not show what P-132's features would give there.
performance_validity: The exclusion does not apply. P-177's accuracy is 0.92, below 0.97; its 0.97 is a specificity, not a discrimination summary. It is small and internal (LOOCV), and the Arizona cohort is analysed separately rather than as external validation, but it does not reach the threshold. P-132's figures are 0.73-0.81.

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon: progression within 7 years (P-132) vs about 2 years (P-177).
candidate_explanations.quote: We utilized the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database to study 175 NC individuals, identifying 50 who progressed to MCI within seven years.

candidate_explanations.difference: Case and control construction: amnestic MCI progressors against age-, sex-, education- and APOE-matched nonprogressors who stayed unimpaired at least 4 years, an extreme-group design, against all eligible NC with 7-year follow-up.
candidate_explanations.quote: From ADNI-1, ADNI-2, ADNI-Go, and ADNI-3 we found 60 participants who developed clinically significant memory impairment, i.e. aMCI, in approximately 2 years and 60 age, sex, education and APOE-matched nonprogressors who remained cognitively unimpaired for at least 4 years.

candidate_explanations.difference: Scan timing: P-177's progressor scans are selected 2 years before diagnosis, and the matched nonprogressor scans correspond to them.
candidate_explanations.quote: "Baseline" scans were the MRI scans from progressors at 2 years prior to clinically significant decline and the corresponding matched nonprogressors' MRI scans.

candidate_explanations.difference: Class balance: 125 stable vs 50 progressors (P-132) against 60 vs 60 (P-177), which changes what an accuracy measures.
candidate_explanations.quote: A total of 175 individuals were enrolled, with 125 sNC and 50 pNC

candidate_explanations.difference: Features: radiomic features plus ADAS-Cog scores (P-132) vs surface multivariate morphometry with patch-based sparse coding (P-177).
candidate_explanations.quote: we incorporated the scores of the ADAS-cog11 and ADAS-cog13 scales, which showed substantial group disparities at baseline, as crucial elements in the final set of modeling features.

candidate_explanations.difference: Representation within P-177's own design: hippocampal volume gives 0.72 against 0.92 for surface MMS on the same ADNI sample.
candidate_explanations.quote: prediction of aMCI using baseline hippocampal volume, random forest classification with leave-one-out cross-validation in the same data sets yielded only 79% prediction accuracy in the Arizona cohort and 72% in the ADNI cohort (Table 4).

candidate_explanations.difference: Validation: a 35-subject held-out test split (P-132) against leave-one-out CV over the 120 subjects whose patches also build the sparse-coding dictionary. P-177 does not say whether the dictionary was learned inside the folds.
candidate_explanations.quote: The dictionary was initialized by randomly selecting patches,[43] which has proved to be an efficient method in practice, and then we started learning the dictionary and sparse codes by Stochastic Coordinate Coding.

candidate_explanations.difference: Sample size, which the authors name as a limitation.
candidate_explanations.quote: Limitations of this study include relatively small numbers of progressors and non-progressors in both cohorts and thus this method will need to be replicated in other, larger data sets.

reason: Both papers predict progression from normal cognition to MCI in ADNI from baseline hippocampal MRI and report accuracy, and neither prints a figure under the other's condition. The gap clears uncertainty in both directions: P-177's 0.92 lies outside P-132's Wilson intervals (upper bound 0.879 even for its best test model), and P-132's test accuracies (0.73-0.77) and training accuracies (0.79-0.81) lie outside P-177's interval (0.853-0.954). A two-sample test gives z = 2.23 against 0.743 and z = 1.93 against 0.771. The candidate explanations are horizon, amnestic-MCI cases against extreme-group matched controls, scan timing, class balance, features and validation. None is shown to be sufficient; P-177's volume baseline shows representation matters in its own design but does not test P-132's features. The record's 'Acc 79' is P-132's training figure; the test figure (0.74) widens the gap.
